extracted.intended_audience: authors and advanced users of plain TeX (TeX macro writers and typesetters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and low-level rules for how plain TeX breaks pages, handles insertions (figures/footnotes), and uses numeric/box registers; intended for users implementing or debugging TeX layouts and macros. Covers permissible breakpoints, penalties, helper macros ( ilbreak, 	opinsert,  ootnote, etc.), tracing, and register/box semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \eject to force a page break (beware stretching)
rubrics_metrics.description: To force the machine to break at your favorite place, type '\eject'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful: \eject will cause TEX to stretch the page out, if necessary, so that the top and bottom baselines agree with those on other pages. If you want to eject a short page, filling it with blank space at the bottom, type '\vfill\eject' instead. If you say '\eject' in the middle of a paragraph, the paragraph will end first (as if you typed '\par\eject').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \vfill\eject for short (empty-bottom) pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to eject a short page and fill it with blank space at the bottom, type '\vfill\eject'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids undesirable stretching that plain '\eject' may cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \vadjust{\eject} to force break after current line in mid-paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: You can say '\vadjust{\eject}' in mid-paragraph to force a page break after whatever line contains your current position when the full paragraph is eventually broken into lines; the rest of the paragraph will go on the following page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike plain '\eject' mid-paragraph (which ends the paragraph first), '\vadjust{\eject}' attaches the eject to the current line's break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent immediate page break with \nobreak in vertical mode
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent a page break, you can say '\nobreak' in vertical mode; it inhibits a break at glue that immediately follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: say \nobreak between the title of a subsection and the first line of text. Note: \nobreak does not cancel the effect of other commands like \eject that tell TEX to break; it only inhibits breaks at immediately-following glue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page breaking is a local optimization (one page at a time)
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX breaks lists of lines into pages by computing badness ratings and penalties, but pages are made up one at a time and removed from TEX's memory; there is no looking ahead to see how one page break will affect the next one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEX chooses each page break locally rather than globally (unlike paragraph line breaking which can find optimum breakpoints across the whole paragraph). This limitation can cause suboptimal-looking page breaks if the format is too strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main vertical list item types
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything you contribute to pages is placed on the main vertical list; each item is one of: a box (hbox/vbox/rule); a whatsit; a mark; an insertion; glue (or \leaders); a kern; or a penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glue, kern, and penalty items are called discardable. Vertical lists differ from horizontal ones: character boxes, discretionary breaks, \vadjust items, and math shifts cannot appear in vertical lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible page breakpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Page breaks can occur only at: (a) glue provided that the glue is immediately preceded by a non-discardable item (box/whatsit/mark/insertion); (b) a kern provided that the kern is immediately followed by glue; (c) a penalty (possibly inserted automatically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interline glue is usually inserted automatically between boxes, so there is usually a valid breakpoint between boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty semantics and numeric thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Each potential breakpoint has an associated penalty: high for undesirable breaks, negative for desirable ones. Penalty is zero at glue and kern breaks; nonzero only at explicit penalty breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '\penalty-100' indicates TEX should try to break here. A penalty of 10000 or more inhibits breaking; a penalty of -10000 or less forces breaking. Penalty magnitudes are combined with badness to compute page cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain TeX convenience break macros and their penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX provides \smallbreak, \medbreak, \bigbreak with penalties -50, -100, -200 respectively; they also insert \smallskip/\medskip/\bigskip if a break is not taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands do not increase existing glue unnecessarily (e.g., won't add extra skip after a display). They are convenient before/after theorem statements. \goodbreak is an abbreviation for '\par\penalty-500' and is useful in proofreading to improve subsequent pages without as drastic effect as \eject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \filbreak to prefer paragraph breaks between pages
rubrics_metrics.description: \filbreak roughly means 'Break the page here and fill the bottom with blank space, unless there is room for more copy that is itself followed by \filbreak.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise expansion: '\vfil\penalty-200\vfilneg'. If break is taken at the penalty, preceding \vfil fills bottom of page; if not taken, \vfil and \vfilneg cancel. Putting \filbreak at ends of paragraphs makes page breaks occur between paragraphs when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \raggedbottom to permit variable bottom margins
rubrics_metrics.description: \raggedbottom tells TEX to permit a small amount of variability in bottom margins on different pages to make other spacing uniform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical analog of \raggedright; helps reduce strictness of page format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute page cost from badness, penalty, and insert penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX figures the 'cost' c of a page break using a formula that depends on b (badness of the page), p (penalty at breakpoint), and q (\insertpenalties), with special cases (including infinite badness leading to c=∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical badness is between 0 and 10000, except ∞ for overfull boxes. The cost formula determines whether a breakpoint is remembered as the best so far or whether TEX seizes the initiative to break immediately (e.g., when c=∞ or p ≤ -10000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \tracingpages=1 to debug page-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Set \tracingpages=1 to instruct TEX to put page-cost calculations into your log file; the log shows '%%' line (goal height/max depth) and '%' lines for legal breakpoints with t,g,b,p,c values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: t = total height so far, g = goal height (\vsize), b = badness, p = penalty, c = cost; '#' marks the best breakpoint so far. The trace helps diagnose poor breaks and parameter effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of log parameters: \vsize, \maxdepth, \topskip
rubrics_metrics.description: The '%%' line records the goal height and max depth (saved when first box/insertion enters the current page). \topskip glue is special glue inserted before first box so top baseline is placed predictably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: plain TeX sets \vsize=44pc and \maxdepth=2.2pt; \topskip default 10pt. If first box taller than \topskip, a 'vskip0pt plus' glue is inserted. Changes to \vsize and \maxdepth after the first box do not affect the current page, but \topskip is looked at when the first box is being contributed to the current page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect/alter page metrics via \pagetotal and \pagegoal (and relatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can look at t and g values used in page breaking via the hdimeni values '\pagetotal' and '\pagegoal'. TEX also maintains \pagestretch, \pagefilstretch, \pagefillstretch, \pagefilllstretch, \pageshrink, and \pagedepth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing \pagegoal overrides saved \vsize; when current page contains no boxes, pagetotal and relatives are zero and \pagegoal is TEX's largest hdimeni (no effect). The integer q is available as \insertpenalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of repeated break commands and correct ways to create empty lines/pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you say '\eject\eject', the second \eject is ignored because it's equivalent to \penalty-10000 and penalties are discarded after a page break; similarly '\break\break' in a paragraph creates an empty line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these are not good idioms, prefer '\eject\line{}\vfil\eject' for an empty page and '\break\hbox{}\hfil\break' for an empty line to avoid underfull boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pages are post-processed by an output routine
rubrics_metrics.description: When a page is completed it is removed from the main vertical list and passed to an 'output routine' for further processing before final form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can construct and modify the output routine (see Chapter 23) to attach page numbers and headers/footers.

rubrics_metrics.name: If TEX gives awful pages, either force break or relax format/parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: A really awful-looking page usually means no good page break is possible; TEX treats multiple breaks with b >= 10000 as indistinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions: insert an explicit '\eject' or '\vfill\eject', revise manuscript, or modify TEX parameters (inspect \tracingpages output) to relax strictness so better breaks become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \topinsert, \pageinsert, \midinsert for floating vertical insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations can be inserted using '\topinsert hvertical mode materiali \endinsert', '\pageinsert ... \endinsert', and '\midinsert ... \endinsert' with differing placement behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \topinsert: attempt top of current page, else top of next. \pageinsert: material justified to full page size and appears on following page (no bigskip). \midinsert: tries to insert in middle of current page; if enough room it's like '\bigskip\vbox{...}\bigbreak', otherwise converts to \topinsert. Use them in vertical mode (between paragraphs), not inside boxes or other insertions. Consider saying '\goodbreak' before \midinsert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert grouping/local effects inside inserts
rubrics_metrics.description: The vertical-mode material in an insert may contain embedded paragraphs; local settings like '\hsize=3in' and '\raggedright' inside an insert do not extend past the '\endinsert' since grouping is implied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX automatically adds a 'bigskip' below each topinsert to separate caption from text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple topinsert/pageinsert commands retain relative order and may float to later pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have two or more \topinsert or \pageinsert in quick succession, TEX may carry them over to subsequent pages but will retain their relative order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a sequence of inserts of various sizes will be placed on successive pages in order; plan insertion sizes relative to page height to predict placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \vfill\supereject at end to flush remaining insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of a paper (or chapter) to ensure no insertions are lost, use '\vfill\supereject'; plain TeX will flush out remaining insertions, filling bottoms of incomplete pages with blank space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also useful to prevent insertions from floating into following chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote placement and constraints (\footnote macro rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The \footnote macro has two parameters: first the reference mark (appears in paragraph and the footnote), then the text of the footnote. TEX will ensure each footnote occurs at the bottom of the same page as its reference; long footnotes will be split across pages if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote text may be several paragraphs and can contain displayed equations but should not involve other insertions. Authors are advised to avoid footnotes for good exposition (they tend to be distracting). Plain TeX sets footnotes differently from the manual: normal size with \textindent for the mark, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on where to use \footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: The \footnote macro should be used only in paragraphs or hboxes that are contributed to the main vertical list; insertions will be lost if they occur inside of boxes that are inside of boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place a \footnote into a subformula of math. It's acceptable to use footnotes within \centerline or on the outer level of a table entry inside an \halign. For complex cases (footnote in captions inside inserts), use \vfootnote in vertical mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertions cannot appear within insertions; use \vfootnote when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Insertions cannot appear within insertions, so you can't use \footnote within a \topinsert; if you need a footnote in a caption, use \vfootnote in vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In complex circumstances (mixing topinserts and footnotes) rethink format; mixing can lead to overfull vboxes when held-over insertions compete for the same page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migration of vertical-mode material
rubrics_metrics.description: Insertions, marks, and the results of \vadjust migrate from horizontal lists to the enclosing vertical list according to rules explained in Chapter 24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the migration mechanism when designing macros that produce insertions or \vadjust material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register types, capacities, and assignment syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX has 256 registers of each numeric type: \count0..\count255 (integers within ±2^31-1), \dimen0..\dimen255 (hdimeni), \skip0..\skip255 (hgluei), \muskip0..\muskip255 (hmugluei). Assign with '\count<number> = <number>' or similar; arithmetic via '\advance', '\multiply', '\divide'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplication/division only by integers; division discards remainder; don't divide by zero or multiply to exceed capacities. Conversions: \skip -> \dimen drops stretch/shrink; \dimen -> number assumes sp units; registers may be used in contexts of the corresponding type (e.g. '\hskip\skip1').

rubrics_metrics.name: Glue arithmetic rules and infinity precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: If infinite glue components are added, lower-order infinities disappear (e.g., adding '2fill' and '1fil' results in '2fill' dominating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after certain \skip assignments and advances, the resulting glue keeps the highest-order infinity components. Understand ordering of fil, fill, filll, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers obey grouping; use \global to persist changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Registers obey TeX's group structure: changes inside {...} do not affect values outside unless \global is used when changing the value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This effectively provides more than 256 registers because group-local changes can be temporary. Use '\global' to make changes persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved count registers for page identification (\count0..\count9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first ten \count registers (\count0..\count9) are displayed on the terminal and transmitted to the output file when outputting a page as page identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX uses \count0 for the page number and keeps \count1..\count9 zero. Ten counts are shipped out so more structured page IDs are possible in complex applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \countdef, \dimendef, \skipdef, \muskipdef for symbolic register names
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX provides '\countdef\chapno=28' to make '\chapno' an abbreviation for '\count28'; similarly for dimensions and skips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After \countdef a control sequence can be used like an integer parameter (e.g., \tolerance). This aids readability and macro design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box registers: \setbox, \box consumes contents, use \copy to preserve
rubrics_metrics.description: Box registers \box0..\box255 hold hboxes or vboxes. '\setbox< n>=<hbox>' sets a box. When you use '\box' it puts the contents into the list and makes the register void; '\copy' preserves the box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to use a box without wiping it out, use '\copy'. Unboxing with '\unhbox' or '\unvbox' also annihilates the register and removes one level of boxing. Prefer '\unhbox'/'\unvbox' or their copy variants for building large boxes by accretion to save memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unboxing semantics and outer glue behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: An unboxing operation 'unsets' any glue that was set at the box's outer level; glue inside nested inner boxes remains unaffected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: making a box 5% wider via '\unhcopy' causes outer glue to stretch, inner box glue does not change. Understand void vs empty box: void register allows \unhbox/\unvbox even if void; an empty box is an actual box with zero dims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box registers are local to groups; global\setbox behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Box registers are local to groups like other registers; using '\global\setbox< n>=<box>' makes the register globally set but it will become 'globally void' when subsequently used or unboxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with global box usage and the semantics of void vs empty boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive nested boxes; use \unhbox/\unvbox when building large boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you construct a large box by accretion inefficiently you may nest boxes deeply and exhaust memory; best to use '\unhbox' or '\unvbox' to append material rather than nesting boxes inside boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs show the memory difference between nested boxing vs unboxing-and-appending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging registers and boxes with \showthe, \showbox, and \tracingall
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '\showthe\count1', '\showthe\dimen2', '\showthe\skip3' to display register contents; '\showbox4' to display box contents. '\tracingall' turns on every tracing mode including '\tracingonline'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box contents appear in the log unless '\tracingonline=1' is set. These features help check register and box behavior while developing macros or answering exercises.
